spec.title: Frame footprint: meta files move into .frame/, delivery stays native

tasks.title: Add src/main/frameStore.js and the new frameConstants entries
tasks.whatChanged: New src/main/frameStore.js owns the overlay/legacy resolution rule and the projectPath-keyed typed API (tasks, notes, structure, quickstart, agents, config, projectId, metaDir, isLegacyLayout), reading from disk and writing through fsSafe.writeFileAtomic. src/shared/frameConstants.js gains CLAUDE_RULE_PATH, FRAME_GITIGNORE_FILE, LEGACY_SYMLINKS, MIGRATION_BACKUP_DIR and FRAME_FILE_CLASSES, and drops FRAME_FILES.GEMINI_SYMLINK. test/frameStore.test.js covers the rule, the fingerprint gate, the round-trips, the .bak and the identity stamp.
tasks.whyChanged: getTasks returns fsSafe's { data, source, error } record because tasksManager renders a different UI for 'restored from .bak' than for unrecoverable corruption; flattening it would push tasksManager back to reading the file itself. resolvePath is exported so migration and the IPC layer get the same answer without re-joining .frame/. frameProject.js's two GEMINI.md references were pointed at a local constant so the dropped FRAME_FILES entry does not break init before T04 removes that block.

tasks.title: Route every meta-file caller through the seam
tasks.whatChanged: tasksManager takes its path from frameStore.resolvePath, reads via frameStore.getTasks, writes via frameStore.saveTasks and watches frameStore.metaDir(projectPath) with the filename === 'tasks.json' check intact, plus a new restartWatching(projectPath) for T09 to call after a migration. overviewManager's loadStructure/loadTasks/loadDecisions and frameProject's spec-driven AGENTS.md reads and writes go through the store; specManager's tasks.json watcher resolves its path the same way. New LOAD_STRUCTURE_MAP channel, handled by frameStore.setupIPC (registered in src/main/index.js), lets src/renderer/structureMap.js drop its fs/path requires and invoke instead.
tasks.whyChanged: The watcher now keys on the meta directory rather than the project path so a layout change re-arms instead of silently watching the wrong directory, and the parse-once cache keeps its mtime+size key (the perf spec's) by asking frameStore for the resolved path. test/tasksManager.test.js and test/specTasksSync.test.js moved their fixtures into .frame/ because a bare root tasks.json with no config.files record is deliberately not Frame's file any more; a new tasksManager case pins that an unmigrated project still reads and writes its root copy.

tasks.title: Scripts resolve their own project root; hooks stage .frame/STRUCTURE.json
tasks.whatChanged: update-structure.js, find-module.js and check-freshness.js each resolve the project the way spec-index.js does (FRAME_PROJECT_ROOT wins, then .frame/bin two up, then scripts/.., then cwd) and take meta paths from a local resolveMetaPath that prefers .frame/, falls back to an existing root file and never creates one at the root; update-structure.js mkdirs .frame/ before writing. .githooks/pre-commit and frameTemplates.getStructureHookSnippet stage .frame/STRUCTURE.json when it exists and the root copy otherwise, and structureBootstrap's lefthook instructions name the .frame/ path. New test/scriptsProjectRoot.test.js stages the scripts with the real copyParserScripts and runs all three with no env.
tasks.whyChanged: check-freshness needed resolveMetaPath to return the root-relative form as well, because its QUICKSTART staleness check passes the path to git as a pathspec. The js-src-app fixture keeps its golden at the project root, so test/projectAgnostic.test.js now covers both halves of the rule: that fixture exercises the legacy fallback while the other five, having no root copy, assert the parser writes .frame/STRUCTURE.json.

tasks.title: Init writes the new layout, delivered natively
tasks.whatChanged: frameTemplates: AGENTS/REFERENCE templates on .frame/ paths with the pointer note replacing the symlink note, config template with projectId and settings.gitSharing and no files record, new getClaudeRuleTemplate() and getFrameGitignoreBlock(), SPEC_HINT_HOOKS moved here in the guarded sh -c form (plus LEGACY_SPEC_HINT_COMMANDS for migration), Codex/generic wrappers on .frame/AGENTS.md. frameProject.runProjectInit writes only .frame/* plus .claude/rules/frame.md via the new ensureClaudePointer, stamps the id with frameStore.ensureProjectId, and installs hooks through installSpecHintHook(projectPath, {file}) chosen by sharing mode; createSymlinkSafe, the consume block and every GEMINI.md path are gone, and removeSpecHintHook lands for T10. The sample project moved to the new layout. New tests: frameProjectInit.test.js (10) and nativeContext.test.js.
tasks.whyChanged: Re-init now carries over the existing projectId and gitSharing instead of rewriting config.json from the template, because a fresh UUID on every init would break the identity the cloud layer is supposed to anchor on. The sample-project conversion (nominally T05) landed here because the init suite's no-legacy-fingerprint case asserts it. nativeContext.test.js skips rather than fails without the CLI, and it really ran here: claude -p returned both codewords, proving criterion 3.

tasks.title: User-facing layout surfaces follow the new layout
tasks.whatChanged: index.html's init modal lists the .frame/ files and the pointer, states that nothing is added to the project root and that Claude Code must be new enough to load .claude/rules/ (2.1.x; /context confirms), and carries the repo-pre-selected sharing radios for T07 to wire; panels.css styles the note, requirement and sharing rows. frameProject.checkExistingFrameFiles now lists only Frame's own paths and the confirmation text lost the CLAUDE.md-consumption paragraph. The renderer's "Created:" line, sampleBanner's strings and the static src/templates/CLAUDE.md name .frame/ paths; both spotlight cards list the .frame/ files.
tasks.whyChanged: checkExistingFrameFiles no longer reports a root CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md as a conflict, because init neither reads nor replaces them — listing them would describe a collision that cannot happen any more. The minimum-version note names the 2.1.x line and tells the user to run /context rather than asserting an exact build number that cannot be verified from here.

tasks.title: Sharing mode: gitExclude and gitSharing
tasks.whatChanged: New src/main/gitExclude.js owns Frame's marker block in the file named by `git rev-parse --git-path info/exclude`, with anchored entries carrying `show-prefix` for sub-directory projects, tracked detection via `git ls-files --cached -- .frame/`, user lines preserved and a stated no-op outside git. New src/main/gitSharing.js reads and writes settings.gitSharing, regenerates the managed .frame/.gitignore block from the file classes (STRUCTURE.json excluded from it, per the tracked decision), moves the spec-hint hook entries between .claude/settings.json and settings.local.json, and returns { mode, tracked, inGit, warning, hookFile } for the UI. 13 new tests across test/gitExclude.test.js and test/gitSharing.test.js.
tasks.whyChanged: ensureExcluded actively withdraws an existing block when .frame/ is tracked rather than just declining to add one, because tracked state changes behind Frame's back the moment someone commits .frame/ — that is also why gitSharing.reconcile() exists for project open and post-migration. A tracked .frame/ under `local` stores the preference and hands the UI the `git rm -r --cached` command; Frame never runs it.

tasks.title: Sharing mode wired into the UI
tasks.whatChanged: Added GET_GIT_SHARING_STATE and SET_GIT_SHARING (plus the migration and remove channels T09/T10 need) to ipcChannels, handled in frameProject.setupIPC through gitSharing; CHECK_IS_FRAME_PROJECT now also answers layout: none|legacy|overlay. runProjectInit takes the mode from the init modal (state.js reads the checked radio) and calls gitSharing.reconcile so the exclude block and .frame/.gitignore land at init. Settings → Workflow gained a Git-sharing select with a warning line and the Remove Frame row, wired in settingsModal.js with the same ipcRenderer.invoke pattern as the spec-driven toggle, styled in settings-modal.css; index.js calls gitSharing.init({ activityLog }).
tasks.whyChanged: The select renders entirely from main's state object (mode, tracked, inGit, warning, hookFile) rather than tracking its own state, so the tracked-under-local warning cannot drift from what git actually says. The layout answer and the Remove Frame markup landed here rather than in T09/T10 because both are one-line additions to surfaces this task was already rewriting.

tasks.title: layoutMigration: pure plan(), consented run()
tasks.whatChanged: New src/main/layoutMigration.js. plan() is pure: fingerprint (config.files record plus a root file), per-artifact dispositions (move / delete-identical / backup-conflict / backup-only for .bak siblings), Frame-planted symlinks only (target basename AGENTS.md), the restorable CLAUDE.md block, the dirty list from git status --porcelain compared against show-prefix + rel, the tracked list and the derived sharing mode. run() backs every file up before touching it, copies via fsSafe and byte-verifies before unlinking, restores CLAUDE.md verbatim, makes targeted AGENTS.md line edits with a review list for anything it could not find, writes the pointer, stamps the id, drops the files record, replaces the unguarded hook entries, applies the sharing mode and refreshes .frame/bin. Added migration.* and sharing.mode_changed to the activity registry. 13 tests in test/layoutMigration.test.js.
tasks.whyChanged: Untracked files are deliberately NOT dirty: in an unshared project every meta file is untracked, so counting them would make migration impossible exactly where it is safest — only tracked modifications defer. Two bugs the tests caught: porcelain lines must be matched, not sliced at a fixed column (the git helper trims, which shifts the first line by one char), and sharing.mode_changed had to be registered or the activity layer would silently drop T06's record.

tasks.title: Migration consent wired end to end
tasks.whatChanged: GET_LAYOUT_MIGRATION_PLAN and RUN_LAYOUT_MIGRATION are handled in frameProject.setupIPC, streaming LAYOUT_MIGRATION_PROGRESS to the sender and calling tasksManager.restartWatching after a successful run; index.js inits layoutMigration with the activity log. New src/renderer/migrationModal.js renders four states from one modal (plan, progress, receipt, dirty-tree deferral) with markup in index.html and styles in ui.css, and state.js offers it when IS_FRAME_PROJECT_RESULT carries layout: 'legacy'. Three more tests cover the plan payload shape, the none/legacy/overlay answer, and that Later leaves the project untouched and working.
tasks.whyChanged: The modal remembers a Later per project for the session rather than persisting it: the offer should come back next launch (the layout is still wrong) but never twice while the user is working. Progress goes to event.sender rather than the main window so the reply lands in the window that asked, and the run is driven from main's own fresh plan() so a stale renderer plan can never be executed.

tasks.title: Remove Frame from a project
tasks.whatChanged: frameProject.removeFrame deletes .frame/, .claude/rules/frame.md (and the rules/ directory when Frame's file was the only thing in it), Frame's hook entries from both Claude settings files via removeSpecHintHook, the marker block in .git/hooks/pre-commit or .husky/pre-commit, and the exclude block, then calls workspace.removeProject; REMOVE_FRAME_FROM_PROJECT is handled in setupIPC and pushes a fresh workspace list. The Settings → Workflow button confirms first, naming exactly what is deleted, then reports the returned list. Two tests: no Frame bytes remain and every user file is checksum-equal, and hooks/pre-commit content the user wrote survives.
tasks.whyChanged: The exclude block is removed before .frame/ because it names that directory. Stripping the pre-commit block also takes back the blank-line separator Frame's appender inserted — without that the user's .husky/pre-commit came back one byte different, which the checksum test caught; and a hook file left with nothing but a shebang was Frame's own creation, so it is deleted rather than left as a stub.

tasks.title: Prose follows the layout
tasks.whatChanged: Pointed the orchestration templates (CONDUCTOR.md, WORKER.md), the spec command templates (spec.implement/tasks/plan.md) and orchestrationManager's merge-reconcile message at .frame/ paths, and rewrote the layout sections of README.md, docs/index.html and docs/capabilities/index.html around the .frame/ directory, the .claude/rules/frame.md pointer, the sharing modes and the Claude Code minimum version. Removed the last public claims that Frame symlinks CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md.
tasks.whyChanged: Prose only, no behaviour. The docs' Gemini entries described a symlink Frame no longer creates, so they now describe what is actually true — plain files under .frame/ that any CLI can be pointed at — rather than naming a tool Frame has stopped integrating with.

tasks.title: Dogfood: migrate this repository
tasks.whatChanged: Ran layoutMigration.plan()/run() headlessly against this repo (Electron stubbed the way the tests do). AGENTS.md, STRUCTURE.json, PROJECT_NOTES.md, tasks.json and QUICKSTART.md moved into .frame/ with byte-equal copies in .frame/migration-backup/ (tasks.json.bak travelled with them), the CLAUDE.md symlink is gone, .claude/rules/frame.md and .frame/.gitignore are written, config.json lost its files record and gained projectId + settings.gitSharing: repo. npm test (286), npm run structure (116 modules into .frame/STRUCTURE.json), spec-context.js and find-module.js all pass against the migrated layout.
tasks.whyChanged: The dogfood found a real bug: this repo's symlink note is a two-line blockquote, and the single-line regex left the continuation behind, mangling the paragraph — the matcher now takes the whole note paragraph and preserves its prefix, with a regression test. This repo's own .claude/settings.json hooks call scripts/spec-hint.js rather than the .frame/bin form, so removeSpecHintHook correctly left them alone; the guarded entries migration added on top were reverted to keep this repo's hook wiring exactly as it was.

tasks.title: Fix the sharing-mode engine at init and on open
tasks.whatChanged: Renamed runProjectInit's `gitSharing` local to `sharingMode` — it shadowed the module of the same name, so `gitSharing.reconcile()` threw into a swallowing catch and no init ever wrote `.frame/.gitignore` or the exclude block. CHECK_IS_FRAME_PROJECT now reconciles the stored mode on every project open. gitExclude gained per-project markers (a sub-directory project qualifies them with its `show-prefix`), a whole-line/CRLF/EOF-safe `splitBlock` that gitSharing reuses for `.frame/.gitignore`, and `/.claude/settings.local.json` among the excluded entries. `gitSharing.setMode` refuses a non-object config, writes config.json only when the mode actually changes, and returns the `installSpecHintHook` result as `hooks`.
tasks.whyChanged: The marker block is per repository but Frame is per project, so two projects in one monorepo were rewriting each other's block; qualifying the markers with the prefix (root keeps the historical plain form, so existing blocks are still recognised) was the smallest fix that keeps both. Config is written conditionally because reconcile now runs on every open and had no business rewriting config.json and its .bak each time.

tasks.title: Make the hook guard exit 0 and preserve user formatting
tasks.whatChanged: The hook command is now `sh -c '[ ! -f .frame/bin/spec-hint.js ] || exec node …'`; the old `&&` forms joined LEGACY_SPEC_HINT_COMMANDS so removal still recognises them. `installSpecHintHook`/`removeSpecHintHook` detect the settings file's own indentation and write it back, and install now declines when a hook already runs spec-hint.js by any route Frame does not currently install.
tasks.whyChanged: With `&&` a missing spec-hint.js made the whole `sh -c` exit 1, so a clone without .frame/bin reported a failing hook on every prompt — the test now actually runs both commands in an empty directory. Treating Frame's own older command as 'already wired' is what stops the mixed-entry state the dogfood hit by hand: migration removes the known forms first, so anything left really is the user's.

tasks.title: Ship .frame/bin with the project
tasks.whatChanged: Moved `bin/` from the runtime class into `derived`, and added FRAME_TRACKED_DERIVED (STRUCTURE.json, bin/) as the list the managed `.frame/.gitignore` block leaves out. `copyParserScripts` is copy-if-changed (commandStaging.copyIfChanged) and, together with `stageCommandFiles`, now runs from the CHECK_IS_FRAME_PROJECT handler so an older checkout heals on open. The pre-commit snippet falls back to the main worktree's parser via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` while still writing the current checkout's STRUCTURE.json. This repository's `.frame/bin` is staged and the root `.gitignore` line that hid it is gone.
tasks.whyChanged: A linked worktree — every orchestration worker — has no `.frame/bin` of its own, so the hook resolved a parser that was not there and silently did nothing; committing `bin/` fixes the common case and the common-dir fallback covers checkouts that predate it. Staging on open had to become copy-if-changed first: rewriting ten identical files on every project selection would churn watchers and mtimes.

tasks.title: Stop spec-phase regression when task data is unavailable
tasks.whatChanged: `derivePhase` returns `currentPhase` unchanged when `tasksDataOrNull` is null or undefined, so `reconcilePhase` cannot rewrite a status.json on the strength of task data it never read. Exported `reconcilePhase` for the regression test in test/specTasksSync.test.js, restored the 19 status.json files this repository's working tree had already been walked back in, and added the upgrade note to README plus a rule to the spec digest.
tasks.whyChanged: Absence of data is not data: an old Frame build reading the pre-migration root tasks.json found nothing, fell through to the file-based check and walked 21 finished specs from `done` to `tasks_generated`. Keeping the recorded phase is the conservative answer — real task data still rewinds a phase when a task really is pending, which the test pins alongside the null case.

tasks.title: Harden the migration engine
tasks.whatChanged: plan() reads the consumed CLAUDE.md block from the root AGENTS.md directly, and an empty or unparseable .frame/ counterpart gets the new `replace-invalid` disposition (bad overlay to migration-backup/<name>.unusable, root file takes its place). run()'s steps moved into execute() so a throw returns a truthful partial receipt (ran: true, failedAt, what got through) plus a migration.failed event, and the RUN_LAYOUT_MIGRATION handler catches around it, re-arms specManager.startWatching and pushes a fresh file tree. The modal only defers a project the user actually decided about, renders the partial receipt, and dialogs.js replaces a legacy-layout sample-project copy instead of offering to migrate it.
tasks.whyChanged: frameStore.readAgents is overlay-first by design, which is exactly wrong for reading what the *legacy* init wrote — a stray .frame/AGENTS.md meant the user's CLAUDE.md quietly did not come back. The receipt now speaks up in both silent cases (no block found, target already exists). `replace-invalid` is a third disposition rather than a flag so the plan artifact keeps its two-key shape.

tasks.title: Honour D10 and tidy removal
tasks.whatChanged: installPreCommitHook's husky branch returns the snippet as manual instructions instead of writing .husky/pre-commit, and the now-dead appendToHookFile/hasFrameSnippet went with it — Frame writes exactly one hook file, .git/hooks/pre-commit, and only where none exists. removeFrame deletes that file when nothing but Frame's own header and marker block are left (matched against the template, not a loose regex), deletes a settings file that now parses to {}, and the renderer calls the new state.noteFrameRemoved() so the spec panel and toggles see a non-Frame project without the init prompt bouncing back.
tasks.whyChanged: The existing test fixture was not a git repository, so the husky branch never ran in tests and the D10 violation shipped unnoticed; the new fixture sets core.hooksPath and asserts the user's hook is byte-identical. Residue detection compares against what Frame's own template leaves behind rather than 'only comments', so a user hook that happens to be all comments is never deleted.

tasks.title: Make .claude/rules/frame.md an inline copy of .frame/AGENTS.md
tasks.whatChanged: getClaudeRuleTemplate(agentsText) now emits a generated-from header plus the whole of AGENTS.md, and ensureClaudePointer became syncClaudeRule(projectPath) — write-only-when-different — called at init, on project open, after migration, after every spec-driven enable/disable/upgrade, and from tasksManager's meta-directory watcher through the new onMetaFileChange hook. The AGENTS/CLAUDE templates and the migration's note replacement say Claude reads the generated copy; this repo's and the sample project's rule files were regenerated; spec.md D2 records why an import cannot work.
tasks.whyChanged: Verified against the real CLI: from <project>/sub, .claude/rules/frame.md loads but @../../.frame/AGENTS.md is not expanded, so the session got an empty rule — the new sub-directory case in test/nativeContext.test.js now finds the codeword where it previously found NONE. Riding tasksManager's existing watcher rather than opening a second one on the same directory keeps the copy fresh while Frame runs.
